description: Probability quantiser holding two scales at once: the pitches both scales contain always sound, and the pitches only one of them has are let through by chance

params.text: Flips that pitch in the first scale between full chance and none by writing 1 or 0 into its probability knob; the scale's name then reads CUSTOM
Flips that pitch in the second scale between full chance and none by writing 1 or 0 into its probability knob; the scale's name then reads CUSTOM
Flips that pitch in both scales at once: if either scale has it, both drop it, and if neither has it, both take it
Sets the chance of that pitch in the first scale, 0 for never and 1 for every trigger
Sets the chance of that pitch in the second scale, 0 for never and 1 for every trigger
Scales the chance of the pitches that only the first scale has, and leaves the pitches shared with the second scale alone; it is fully open when the module is added
Scales the chance of the pitches that only the second scale has, and leaves the pitches shared with the first scale alone; it is fully closed when the module is added
Chooses the first scale from a list of 43, chromatic at the bottom, and writes 1 or 0 into all twelve of that scale's probability knobs, losing whatever was set there
Chooses the second scale from a list of 43, chromatic at the bottom, and writes 1 or 0 into all twelve of that scale's probability knobs, losing whatever was set there
Rotates the first scale to a new root, C at the bottom through to B, and writes 1 or 0 into all twelve of that scale's probability knobs, losing whatever was set there
Rotates the second scale to a new root, C at the bottom through to B, and writes 1 or 0 into all twelve of that scale's probability knobs, losing whatever was set there

inputs.text: Steps past the first SCALE knob's setting, the whole list of 43 across 10V, wrapping round the end; the size of the voltage is used and its sign is thrown away
Steps past the second SCALE knob's setting, the whole list of 43 across 10V, wrapping round the end; the size of the voltage is used and its sign is thrown away
The pitch to be quantised; it is read only at the moment a trigger arrives
On each rising edge a fresh random number is drawn for every one of the twelve pitches, and the voltage at IN is quantised against whichever pitches those draws allow
Adds to the first scale's unique-pitch chance, a whole unit per volt, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Adds to the second scale's unique-pitch chance, a whole unit per volt, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Steps past the first KEY knob's setting, all twelve keys across 10V, wrapping round the end; the size of the voltage is used and its sign is thrown away
Steps past the second KEY knob's setting, all twelve keys across 10V, wrapping round the end; the size of the voltage is used and its sign is thrown away
Adds to that pitch's chance in the first scale, a whole unit per volt, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Adds to that pitch's chance in the second scale, a whole unit per volt, and the total is held between 0 and 1

outputs.text: The quantised pitch, held unchanged until the next trigger

notes: Nothing comes out until both IN and TRIGGER are patched, and the output carries the smaller of their two channel counts.
When the random draw allows no pitch at all, the previous pitch is sent again.
The lamp by each first-scale knob shows that pitch’s chance there, the lamp by each second-scale knob its chance in that scale, and the row at the foot the greater of the two.
To move from one scale to the other, close both PROBABILITY knobs, which leaves only the pitches the two share, then set the new scale and open its own PROBABILITY knob.
Quantising works inside one octave and never rounds across the top of it, so a pitch near the octave is pulled down to the nearest allowed pitch below rather than to the one above.
